cover.confidentiality_statement: This document contains information that is confidential and proprietary to Puris Natural Aroma Chemicals (Pty) Ltd (“Puris”). It shall not be disclosed outside Puris, transmitted, duplicated, or used in whole or in part for any purpose other than its intended purpose, without the explicit written permission of Puris. This report reflects the state of the systems, documents and personnel interviewed at the time of the assessment and does not constitute legal advice.

company_profile.location: 25 Textile Street, Riverside Industrial Park, Paarl, Western Cape, South Africa
company_profile.industry: Natural aroma ingredients for the global flavour and fragrance industries
company_profile.activities: Produces and sells essential oils, high-value aroma isolates and single molecules.

objectives: Determine the current compliance posture against POPIA.
Assess the practical human element through structured staff interviews.
methodology: Review of the documents listed in Appendix A.
Line-by-line mapping to POPIA and ISO/IEC 27701:2019.
A 41-question security and privacy awareness interview with four respondents.
limitations: The assessment reflects evidence available at the assessment date.
Under Review controls remain open until sufficient evidence is obtained.
The awareness result reflects one departmental cohort of four people.

outstanding_documents.position: Referenced across the ISMS suite. Backup retention is currently covered at Section 4 of PU-POL-DRP-002 only.
Referenced at Section 8.5 of PU-POL-ISM-011. Log retention and review are not defined in a standalone document.
No procedure governs release of personal information to a third party or to law enforcement, and no disclosure log exists.
No classification scheme is in force. Until one exists, handling rules apply uniformly to all information.
No documented change process for IT systems. The FSSC 22000 SOP discipline in production is the model to copy.
Referenced by the mobile and access control policies. Remote working is currently governed by PU-POL-MOB-015 as an interim measure.
Referenced by PU-POL-ACC-012. Supplier access is currently governed by Section 4.2 of that policy with PU-AGR-DPA-006.

implementation_programme.title: Governance activation
implementation_programme.owner: Outsourced DIO, with Executive Chairman and Managing Director decisions
actions: Board adoption of PU-POL-POPIA-001 and PU-POL-ISM-011, recorded in the minutes.
Registration of the Information Officer with the Information Regulator, and issue of the written section 56 designation for the Deputy.
Naming of the IT function and a deputy, and recording of both in the ISMS governance table and at Annex B of the Incident Response Plan.
POPIA and information security added as a standing board and management agenda item.
Policy register populated and the review cycle started.
implementation_programme.dependencies: Must complete first; governance appointments and the named IT function are preconditions to most of the programme.

implementation_programme.title: Records foundation
implementation_programme.owner: Outsourced DIO, with IT for system interrogation
actions: Build the Record of Processing Activities from the system register at Annex A of PU-POL-POPIA-001.
Identify every category of special personal information, document the applicable section 27 to 33 condition and test access restriction.
Complete the lawful-basis column and write a legitimate-interest assessment for each section 11(1)(f) activity.
Map every cross-border flow, confirm Microsoft 365 tenant data residency with evidence and put a section 72 mechanism in place per destination.
Design and apply a classification scheme across the asset register and document libraries.
Build the IT asset register, recording encryption status and owner against every device.
implementation_programme.dependencies: Precedes much of Workstream 3 and meaningful assurance because lawful basis, transfers, retention and operator scoping depend on the ROPA.

implementation_programme.title: Third-party contracting
implementation_programme.owner: Outsourced DIO, with Financial Manager and legal input
actions: Identify the payroll and HR administration provider and execute an operator agreement.
Issue PU-FORM-OCQ-008 to each of the nine operators, assess responses and execute PU-AGR-DPA-006 or accept an adequate vendor equivalent.
Amend the employment contract template to include a post-employment personal information clause and issue variations.
Confirm the cyber insurance and forensic or incident-response arrangements and record both at Annex B of PU-PLN-IRP-019.
implementation_programme.dependencies: Operator scoping and contracting depend on the records foundation and named internal decision-makers.

implementation_programme.title: Technical control build
implementation_programme.owner: IT function — cannot be delivered by the DIO
actions: Extend multi-factor authentication to full coverage across Microsoft 365, administrative accounts and externally reachable services.
Provide and deploy an approved password manager with training.
Audit endpoint encryption across the fleet and remediate exceptions.
Provision a sanctioned remote-access route and supersede the interim public Wi-Fi rule.
Restrict unsanctioned cloud storage and personal-account use at tenant level.
Verify retention periods against configured systems; define and evidence backup retention tiers and restore testing.
Define log retention and review, including at least 12 months for authentication and privileged access logs.
Write and operate patching and IT change standards; audit and restrict local administrator rights.
Implement structured consent capture where consent is relied on.
implementation_programme.dependencies: Runs in parallel and independently, but requires the IT function named under R24.

implementation_programme.title: Operating the cycle
implementation_programme.owner: Outsourced DIO, with IT for the tabletop exercise
actions: Deliver induction and annual awareness training to every employee and temporary worker and retain the attendance register.
Publish the breach reporting route, open the breach register and run a business-email-compromise tabletop exercise.
Write and adopt the third-party disclosure procedure and open the disclosure log.
Record the August 2026 clearance exercise retrospectively and operate the Destruction Register.
Open the DSAR register.
implementation_programme.dependencies: Relies on governance ownership and IT participation for the tabletop exercise; then continues as the standing monthly cycle.

implementation_programme.title: Assurance completion
actions: Extend the Security and Privacy Awareness Interview to the six functions not yet assessed.
Complete Security of Personal Data, Requests for Personal Data and Direct Marketing.
Re-issue this report at version 3.0 with the full control population and a revised maturity rating.
implementation_programme.dependencies: Follows the records foundation and initial implementation so the remaining domains and wider cohort can be assessed against operating evidence.

delivery_options.route: Outsourced Deputy Information Officer, standing engagement
delivery_options.strength: Continuity of the monthly cycle; the registers stay populated; independence from the functions being reviewed
delivery_options.limitation: Cannot deliver Workstream 4. Depends on internal IT and Finance for information and decisions.

delivery_options.route: Defined project, fixed scope and end date
delivery_options.scope: Workstreams 1, 2 and 3 — the build of the ROPA, the contracting programme and the governance activation
delivery_options.strength: Concentrated effort on the foundation items; a clear completion point
delivery_options.limitation: Leaves Workstream 5 without an owner once the project closes, which is where compliance programmes usually decay.

delivery_options.route: Internal IT or the appointed MSP
delivery_options.strength: The only route to closing the technical items
delivery_options.limitation: Requires the IT function to be named first (R24). Scope and accountability should be recorded in the service agreement.

delivery_options.route: Combination — project for the build, standing DIO for the cycle
delivery_options.strength: Matches the shape of the work: the foundation is a project, the operation is a cycle
delivery_options.limitation: Requires clarity at handover on which items transfer and what evidence accompanies them.

delivery_cadence.evidence: Review records with exceptions and actions

residual_exposures.why_it_matters: The notice currently live tells data subjects that Puris may transfer their information outside South Africa — which Puris cannot presently support with a section 72 mechanism — and that it may retain personal information indefinitely, which is not sustainable under section 14. PU-NOT-DPN-007 has been written to replace it and has not yet been published.

Four are already disclosed in that same notice. Puris has told data subjects these disclosures occur without the section 21 contracts governing them, and has no contractual right to breach notification from any supplier.
Every member of staff interviewed had shared a password or MFA code, and MFA coverage is partial. This is the most likely route to a reportable incident.

residual_exposures.exposure: Personal accounts and removable media in use
residual_exposures.why_it_matters: Puris personal information currently sits outside the estate, where it is not backed up, not retained to schedule, not searchable for an access request and not recoverable when a person leaves.
A procedure now exists but has never been exercised, the IT function is unnamed, and cyber insurance and forensic support are unconfirmed. All three matter in the first hours of an incident.
Puris cannot answer the first question the Regulator asks, and cannot scope a data subject access request or a breach with confidence.

residual_exposures.exposure: Special personal information without documented conditions
residual_exposures.why_it_matters: Medical certificates, injury-on-duty records and race data for verification are processed. The condition is now documented in policy; the identification exercise and access restriction are not done.

risk_register.finding: No board-approved, ISO 27701-aligned Privacy Information Management System (PIMS) / governance framework in place
risk_register.recommended_action: Establish a PIMS per ISO 27701 cl.5.2; obtain board endorsement; map to all eight POPIA conditions (30 days)

risk_register.finding: Privacy Policy not yet confirmed as board-approved and mapped to all eight POPIA conditions
risk_register.recommended_action: Finalise, version-control and obtain board sign-off on the POPIA Compliance Policy (30 days)

risk_register.finding: PAIA Manual / Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) currency not confirmed
risk_register.recommended_action: Update and publish the PAIA Manual with a complete RoPA; submit to the Information Regulator (30 days)

risk_register.finding: No documented, role-based POPIA / privacy awareness training programme
risk_register.recommended_action: Roll out mandatory onboarding and annual refresher training, tracked to completion (60 days)

risk_register.finding: Breach recognition and reporting awareness only partially embedded among staff
risk_register.recommended_action: Publish a breach-reporting procedure and run a tabletop exercise (60 days)

risk_register.finding: Lawful basis not consistently mapped per processing activity
risk_register.recommended_action: Complete the RoPA lawful-basis column; document legitimate-interest assessments where relied upon (60 days)

risk_register.finding: Consent capture not consistently freely given, specific and separately recorded
risk_register.recommended_action: Implement structured consent capture (timestamp, purpose, channel, wording version) and quarterly audit (60 days)

risk_register.finding: Special personal information categories not mapped to a documented s.27 condition (staff-related category identified during fieldwork)
risk_register.recommended_action: Identify all special-PI categories; document the applicable s.27 condition; apply heightened controls (60 days)

risk_register.finding: No confirmed lawful mechanism for cross-border transfers of personal information
risk_register.recommended_action: Map all cross-border flows; confirm adequacy or implement standard contractual clauses per destination (90 days)

risk_register.finding: No operator register or POPIA-compliant Data Processing Agreements with third-party processors
risk_register.recommended_action: Build an operator register; execute DPAs covering processing instructions, security and breach obligations (90 days)

risk_register.finding: No board-approved Record Retention Policy or retention schedule
risk_register.recommended_action: Develop and approve a retention schedule cross-referenced to POPIA and sector legislation (60 days)

risk_register.finding: No consistent trigger for deletion, destruction or de-identification once purpose has lapsed
risk_register.recommended_action: Implement automated or scheduled retention-enforcement rules across key systems (90 days)

risk_register.finding: POPIA / PIMS compliance not a standing board or EXCO agenda item
risk_register.recommended_action: Add as a mandatory standing item; record decisions and actions in minutes (30 days)

risk_register.finding: No documented annual review cycle for privacy policies
risk_register.recommended_action: Establish a policy register with review dates, version history and sign-off (60 days)

risk_register.finding: No confidentiality / acceptable-use agreements carrying a post-employment PI clause
risk_register.recommended_action: Update employment contracts and onboarding packs; confirm at offboarding (60 days)

risk_register.finding: No documented third-party / law-enforcement disclosure procedure or log
risk_register.recommended_action: Introduce a disclosure procedure requiring IO or legal review, with a maintained log (60 days)

risk_register.finding: No classified information asset register mapped to retention periods
risk_register.recommended_action: Implement a data classification policy and apply it across the asset register (90 days)

risk_register.finding: No documented secure destruction procedure for paper and electronic media
risk_register.recommended_action: Formalise a media-sanitisation standard; retain destruction certificates (data clearance exercise already commenced 11 August) (60 days)

risk_register.finding: Credential and MFA-code sharing reported by all staff interviewed
risk_register.recommended_action: Reinforce in training; enforce a strict no-sharing rule; consider technical controls (SSO, conditional access) (30 days)

risk_register.finding: Use of public Wi-Fi without a VPN, and personal email / cloud storage for work information, reported by all or most staff interviewed
risk_register.recommended_action: Deploy a VPN or managed access solution; block unsanctioned storage; reinforce policy in training (60 days)

narrative_templates.scope_methodology: The assessment combined structured interviews, evidence review and line-by-line mapping to POPIA and ISO/IEC 27701.

limitations: The assessment reflects evidence available at the assessment date.
Under Review controls remain open until sufficient evidence is obtained.
The awareness result reflects one departmental cohort of four people.

statuses.label: Compliant
statuses.definition: Evidence confirms the control is designed and operating as required.

statuses.label: Partially Compliant
statuses.definition: The control exists in some form but is inconsistently applied or incompletely evidenced.

statuses.label: Under Review
statuses.definition: Insufficient evidence was available at the time of assessment to confirm status.

statuses.label: Non-Compliant
statuses.definition: No evidence of the control was identified.

risks.definition: Immediate action required — material regulatory, financial or reputational exposure.
Action required within 30 days of the applicable phase.
Monitor and review at the next assessment cycle.

delivery_options.route: Outsourced Deputy Information Officer, standing engagement
delivery_options.strength: Continuity of the monthly cycle; the registers stay populated; independence from the functions being reviewed
delivery_options.limitation: Cannot deliver Workstream 4. Depends on internal IT and Finance for information and decisions.

delivery_options.route: Defined project, fixed scope and end date
delivery_options.scope: Workstreams 1, 2 and 3 — the build of the ROPA, the contracting programme and the governance activation
delivery_options.strength: Concentrated effort on the foundation items; a clear completion point
delivery_options.limitation: Leaves Workstream 5 without an owner once the project closes, which is where compliance programmes usually decay.

delivery_options.route: Internal IT or the appointed MSP
delivery_options.strength: The only route to closing the technical items
delivery_options.limitation: Requires the IT function to be named first (R24). Scope and accountability should be recorded in the service agreement.

delivery_options.route: Combination — project for the build, standing DIO for the cycle
delivery_options.strength: Matches the shape of the work: the foundation is a project, the operation is a cycle
delivery_options.limitation: Requires clarity at handover on which items transfer and what evidence accompanies them.
